newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Jan 21.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
THE CHELSEA PURITANS VS ALAN CLARK

Despite reaching the final selection for the safe Tory seat of Kensington and Chelsea last night, former defence minister Alan Clark faces opposition from Kensington and Chelsea Conservative Association members. The group are having second thoughts about replacing disgraced MP Sir Nicholas Scott with celebrated philanderer Alan Clark.
PARCELFORCE TO GET 100 MILLION STG BOOST

The largest investment in Parcelforce history is set to take place, with the Post Office about to pour 100 million stg into the delivery business, creating 700 jobs. A massive distribution centre will be created in Coventry enabling the group to compete with rivals TNT, Federal Express and DHL.
WICKES HITS A CONTINENTAL SELL-OFF SNAG

Wickes, the building materials business, is having difficulty trying to sell off its European subsidiary. Potential buyers are quibbling over the price, even though Wickes is understood to be prepared to accept less than 10 million stg.
IRELAND ON A BUDGET TIGHTROPE FOR EMU

In today's Irish budget speech, Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn will have to perform a skilled balancing act. He needs to accommodate an electorate eager for tax cuts in an election year without losing the tight fiscal policies needed to rein in inflation and keep Ireland on course for joining Europe's single currency.
